title: My flight is delayed
settingKo: 공항 카운터에서 지연된 항공편에 대해 묻습니다.

lines.text: Excuse me, the screen says my flight to Chicago is delayed. Do you know why?
lines.ko: 실례합니다, 화면에 시카고행 항공편이 지연됐다고 나오는데요. 이유를 아시나요?

lines.text: It's because of bad weather. We expect it to leave in about three hours.
lines.ko: 악천후 때문입니다. 약 3시간 뒤 출발할 것으로 보고 있어요.

lines.text: Three hours? I have a connecting flight, so I'm going to miss it.
lines.ko: 3시간이요? 연결편이 있어서 놓치겠네요.

lines.text: I can put you on the next one and give you a meal voucher.
lines.ko: 다음 편으로 바꿔 드리고 식사 쿠폰도 드릴 수 있어요.

lines.text: That would be great. Thanks for sorting this out.
lines.ko: 그럼 좋죠. 해결해 주셔서 감사합니다.

options: 다음 연결편으로 바꾸고 식사 쿠폰을 준다

response.situationKo: 항공사 직원이 수하물이 도착하지 않았다고 알려 줍니다. 어떻게 할지 물어보세요.
response.prompt: I'm sorry, but it looks like your bag didn't arrive on this flight.

answers.text: Oh no. When do you think it will get here?
answers.noteKo: 언제 도착할지 묻는 가장 자연스러운 반응이에요.

answers.text: Could you deliver it to my hotel when it arrives?
You're kidding. What am I supposed to do now?
I see. Is there a form I need to fill out?

title: At the doctor's
settingKo: 의사에게 며칠째 이어지는 증상을 설명합니다.

lines.text: So, what seems to be the problem today?
lines.ko: 오늘은 어디가 불편하신가요?

lines.text: I've had a sore throat and a bad cough for about four days.
lines.ko: 4일쯤 목이 아프고 기침이 심해요.

lines.text: Have you had a fever or any trouble breathing?
lines.ko: 열이 있거나 숨쉬기 힘든 적이 있었나요?

lines.text: I had a slight fever last night, but I can breathe fine.
lines.ko: 어젯밤에 미열이 있었는데 숨은 잘 쉬어져요.

lines.text: It sounds like a virus. Get plenty of rest and come back if it gets worse.
lines.ko: 바이러스인 것 같네요. 푹 쉬시고 심해지면 다시 오세요.

phrases.en: I've had a sore throat for four days.
Come back if it gets worse.

response.situationKo: 약사가 어떤 증상인지 묻습니다. 어제부터 머리가 아프다고 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, how can I help? What are your symptoms?

answers.text: I've had a terrible headache since yesterday.
My head's been killing me since yesterday. Do you have anything for that?
answers.noteKo: killing me는 많이 아프다는 구어 표현이에요.

answers.text: I have a headache that started yesterday. Could you recommend something?
I've got a splitting headache. Can I have some paracetamol?
answers.noteKo: 미국에서는 paracetamol 대신 acetaminophen이나 Tylenol을 많이 써요.

title: Long time no see
settingKo: 길에서 대학 친구를 우연히 다시 만났습니다.

lines.text: Wait, is that you? I haven't seen you in years!
lines.ko: 잠깐, 너야? 몇 년 만이야!

lines.text: No way! How have you been? You look exactly the same.
lines.ko: 세상에! 어떻게 지냈어? 하나도 안 변했네.

lines.text: Pretty good. I moved back last month after working abroad.
lines.ko: 잘 지냈어. 해외에서 일하다가 지난달에 돌아왔어.

lines.text: We should definitely catch up. Are you free for lunch this week?
lines.ko: 꼭 만나서 얘기하자. 이번 주 점심 시간 돼?

lines.text: Sounds perfect. Let me get your new number.
lines.ko: 완전 좋아. 네 새 번호 좀 알려 줘.

response.situationKo: 오랜만에 만난 친구가 안부를 묻습니다. 근황을 한두 문장으로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi! Long time no see. How have you been?

answers.text: It's been ages! I've been pretty busy with work, but I'm doing well. How about you?
Good to see you! Not much has changed, to be honest.
answers.noteKo: Not much로 특별한 일이 없다고 말해요.

answers.text: I've been very well, thank you. It's lovely to see you again.
Alright, mate? Can't complain. What have you been up to?
answers.noteKo: Can't complain은 그럭저럭 잘 지낸다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Hey! I'm doing great. I just started a new job.

title: Something's broken
settingKo: 세입자가 관리인에게 고장 난 보일러 수리를 요청합니다.

lines.text: Hi, this is Min from apartment 4B. The heating stopped working last night.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 4B호 민이에요. 어젯밤에 난방이 멈췄어요.

lines.text: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is there any hot water?
lines.ko: 아, 그거 큰일이네요. 온수는 나오나요?

lines.text: No, nothing. It's freezing in here, especially in the morning.
lines.ko: 아니요, 아무것도요. 특히 아침에는 여기 너무 추워요.

lines.text: I'll send someone over this afternoon between two and four.
lines.ko: 오늘 오후 2시에서 4시 사이에 사람을 보낼게요.

lines.text: Thanks. I'll make sure I'm home then.
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 그 시간엔 꼭 집에 있을게요.

phrases.en: The heating stopped working last night.
I'll send someone over this afternoon.

response.situationKo: 관리인이 문제가 뭔지 묻습니다. 고장 난 것을 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, I got your message. What's going on with the apartment?

answers.text: The kitchen sink is leaking, and there's water all over the floor.
The washing machine stopped working. Could you send someone to look at it?
answers.noteKo: send someone to look at it은 '봐 줄 사람을 보내 주세요'예요.

answers.text: Hey, the shower won't get hot. It's been like this since Sunday.
The window in the bedroom is broken and it won't close.

title: Canceling a subscription
settingKo: 헬스장 회원권을 해지하려고 상담원과 통화합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'd like to cancel my membership. I'm moving to another city.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 회원권을 해지하고 싶어요. 다른 도시로 이사해서요.

lines.text: I understand. Would you like to pause it for three months instead?
lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 대신 3개월 일시 정지하시는 건 어떠세요?

lines.text: No, thanks. I won't be coming back, so I'd rather cancel it.
lines.ko: 아니요, 괜찮아요. 다시 안 올 거라 해지하는 게 나아요.

lines.text: OK. Your last payment will be on the fifteenth, and then it ends.
lines.ko: 네. 15일이 마지막 결제이고 그다음에 종료돼요.

phrases.en: I'd like to cancel my membership.

response.situationKo: 상담원이 할인을 제안하며 붙잡습니다. 정중하게 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: Before you go, we can offer you fifty percent off for the next three months.

answers.text: Thanks for the offer, but I'd still like to cancel.
answers.noteKo: I'd still like to로 결정을 유지해요.

answers.text: I appreciate it, but I've already decided. Please cancel it.
answers.noteKo: I've already decided는 단호하지만 예의 바른 말이에요.

answers.text: That's nice, but no thanks. I really don't use it anymore.
answers.noteKo: don't use it anymore로 이유를 말해요.

answers.text: No, thank you. Could you send me an email confirming the cancellation?
answers.noteKo: 해지 확인 메일을 꼭 받아 두세요.

title: This is past the return date
settingKo: 반품 기한이 조금 지난 물건을 매장에 가져갑니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'd like to return these headphones. The left side stopped working.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 이 헤드폰 반품하고 싶어요. 왼쪽이 안 들려요.

lines.text: I see. Unfortunately, the thirty-day return period ended last week.
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 아쉽지만 30일 반품 기간이 지난주에 끝났어요.

lines.text: But they're broken, not just something I didn't like. Isn't there a warranty?
lines.ko: 그래도 그냥 마음에 안 드는 게 아니라 고장 난 거잖아요. 보증 기간 없나요?

lines.text: You're right, there's a one-year warranty. We can repair them for free.
lines.ko: 맞아요, 1년 보증이 있어요. 무료로 수리해 드릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The return period ended last week.

response.situationKo: 직원이 반품이 안 된다고 합니다. 다른 방법을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: I'm sorry, but we can't accept returns without a receipt.

answers.text: Is there any way I could exchange it instead?
answers.noteKo: Is there any way는 가능성을 부드럽게 물어요.

answers.text: Could you check your system? I paid with my credit card.
answers.noteKo: 카드 결제 기록으로 찾아 달라고 해요.

answers.text: OK, can I at least get store credit?
I understand, but it was a gift. Could I exchange it for a different size?

title: Opening a bank account
settingKo: 해외에서 은행 계좌를 엽니다.

lines.text: Hi, I just moved here for work and I'd like to open a bank account.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 일 때문에 막 이사 왔는데 계좌를 만들고 싶어요.

lines.text: Sure. I'll need your passport, your visa, and proof of address.
lines.ko: 네. 여권, 비자, 그리고 주소 증명이 필요해요.

lines.text: Would my rental contract work as proof of address?
lines.ko: 임대 계약서로 주소 증명이 될까요?

lines.text: Yes, that's fine. Your debit card will arrive by mail in about a week.
lines.ko: 네, 괜찮아요. 체크카드는 일주일쯤 뒤에 우편으로 도착해요.

phrases.en: I'd like to open a bank account.
Would this work as proof of address?

response.situationKo: 은행 직원이 어떤 계좌가 필요한지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: What kind of account are you looking for?

answers.text: Just a basic checking account for my salary.
I'd like a savings account, and also one for everyday use.
Something with no monthly fee, if possible.
I need an account that I can use to send money to Korea.

title: A small accident
settingKo: 주차장에서 다른 차와 살짝 부딪혀 운전자와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Are you OK? I think you hit my car while backing out.
lines.ko: 괜찮으세요? 후진하시다가 제 차를 박으신 것 같아요.

lines.text: I'm so sorry, I didn't see you. Is there any damage?
lines.ko: 정말 죄송해요, 못 봤어요. 어디 망가졌나요?

lines.text: Just a small scratch on the door, but we should exchange information.
lines.ko: 문에 작은 긁힘만 있는데, 그래도 연락처를 주고받아야겠어요.

lines.text: Of course. Here's my insurance card and my phone number.
lines.ko: 물론이죠. 여기 제 보험 카드랑 전화번호요.

response.situationKo: 상대 운전자가 경찰을 부를지 묻습니다. 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should we call the police, or just handle it through insurance?

answers.text: I think insurance is enough. It's only a small scratch.
Let's just take some photos and handle it through insurance.
To be safe, maybe we should call the police and make a report.
We probably don't need the police. Here's my number if anything comes up.
answers.noteKo: if anything comes up은 '혹시 무슨 일 생기면'이에요.

title: No room for us?
settingKo: 예약한 호텔에 도착했는데 방이 없다고 합니다.

lines.text: I'm very sorry, but we're overbooked tonight and your room isn't available.
lines.ko: 정말 죄송하지만 오늘 밤 초과 예약이라 손님 방이 없어요.

lines.text: But I booked this three months ago. What are we supposed to do?
lines.ko: 3개월 전에 예약했는데요. 저희는 어떡하라는 거죠?

lines.text: We've reserved a room for you at our sister hotel, and we'll pay for the taxi.
lines.ko: 자매 호텔에 방을 잡아 두었고 택시비도 저희가 낼게요.

lines.text: OK, but I'd like a discount on the rest of our stay here.
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 그래도 남은 숙박은 할인을 받고 싶어요.

phrases.en: What are we supposed to do?
I'd like a discount on the rest of our stay.

response.situationKo: 방에 문제가 많아요. 프런트에 방을 바꿔 달라고 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hello, front desk. How can I help you?

answers.text: Hi, the room smells like smoke. Could I move to another room?
answers.noteKo: smells like smoke는 담배 냄새가 난다는 거예요.

answers.text: The room is really noisy because it's next to the elevator. Can I change rooms?
Hey, the AC is broken and it's so hot. Is there another room available?
I'm sorry to call so late, but there's a problem with the room. Could you help me?
answers.noteKo: 늦은 시간에 전화한 걸 먼저 사과해요.

title: I missed my connection
settingKo: 앞 비행기가 늦어 환승편을 놓치고 항공사 카운터에 갑니다.

lines.text: Hi, my first flight was late, so I missed my connection to Seoul.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 첫 비행기가 늦어서 서울행 환승편을 놓쳤어요.

lines.text: Let me check. The next flight is tomorrow morning at eight.
lines.ko: 확인해 볼게요. 다음 비행기는 내일 아침 8시예요.

lines.text: Tomorrow? Will the airline cover a hotel for tonight?
lines.ko: 내일이요? 오늘 밤 호텔은 항공사가 내주나요?

lines.text: Yes, here's a hotel voucher and a meal voucher for dinner.
lines.ko: 네, 여기 호텔 바우처와 저녁 식사 바우처예요.

phrases.en: Will the airline cover a hotel?

response.situationKo: 직원이 내일 저녁 비행기를 제안하지만 너무 늦어요. 더 빠른 편을 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: The next available seat is tomorrow at nine p.m.

answers.text: Is there anything earlier? I have an important meeting tomorrow afternoon.
Could you check other airlines, please? I really need to get there by noon.
Can you put me on standby for the morning flight?
Nine p.m.? That's way too late. Any other options?

title: My bag didn't arrive
settingKo: 도착 공항에서 짐이 나오지 않아 신고합니다.

lines.text: Hi, my suitcase didn't come out. I waited until the belt stopped.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 제 캐리어가 안 나왔어요. 벨트가 멈출 때까지 기다렸어요.

lines.text: I'm sorry. Can you describe it and show me your baggage tag?
lines.ko: 죄송합니다. 가방을 설명해 주시고 수하물 표를 보여 주시겠어요?

lines.text: It's a large gray suitcase with a yellow ribbon on the handle.
lines.ko: 큰 회색 캐리어에 손잡이에 노란 리본이 있어요.

lines.text: It's still in Frankfurt. We'll deliver it to your hotel tomorrow.
lines.ko: 아직 프랑크푸르트에 있어요. 내일 호텔로 배달해 드릴게요.

phrases.en: We'll deliver it to your hotel.

response.situationKo: 직원이 가방이 늦게 온다고 합니다. 당장 필요한 것에 대해 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Your bag should arrive in one or two days.

answers.text: What about my clothes in the meantime? Can I buy some and get reimbursed?
Will the airline pay for basic things like a toothbrush?
Two days? My medicine is in that bag. Is there any way to get it sooner?
answers.noteKo: 급한 이유를 말하면 우선 처리될 수 있어요.

answers.text: OK, but can you send me updates by text?

title: My back is killing me
settingKo: 물리치료사에게 허리 통증을 설명합니다.

lines.text: So tell me, when did the back pain start?
lines.ko: 자, 허리 통증이 언제 시작됐어요?

lines.text: About two weeks ago. I sit at my desk for about ten hours a day.
lines.ko: 2주쯤 전이요. 하루에 열 시간쯤 책상에 앉아 있어요.

lines.text: That's probably the reason. Do you take breaks to stretch?
lines.ko: 그게 원인일 거예요. 쉬면서 스트레칭하세요?

lines.text: Honestly, not really. I forget when I'm busy.
lines.ko: 솔직히 별로요. 바쁘면 잊어버려요.

lines.text: Try to stand up every hour. I'll show you some simple exercises.
lines.ko: 한 시간마다 일어나 보세요. 간단한 운동을 알려 드릴게요.

phrases.en: Do you take breaks to stretch?

response.situationKo: 치료사가 생활 습관을 묻습니다. 평소 생활을 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Tell me a little about your daily routine.

answers.text: I usually work from home and sit on the sofa with my laptop.
I commute for two hours and work at a desk all day.
I don't exercise much, and I spend a lot of time on my phone.
I go to the gym three times a week, but I sit for long hours at work.
answers.noteKo: 좋은 습관과 나쁜 습관을 같이 말해요.

title: I'm so burned out
settingKo: 요즘 지친 친구와 이야기를 나눕니다.

lines.text: You look exhausted. Is everything OK at work?
lines.ko: 너 너무 지쳐 보여. 회사 일은 괜찮아?

lines.text: Not really. I've been working until midnight almost every day.
lines.ko: 아니. 거의 매일 자정까지 일하고 있어.

lines.text: That's way too much. Have you talked to your manager about it?
lines.ko: 그건 너무 심하다. 팀장한테 얘기해 봤어?

lines.text: Not yet. I don't want them to think I can't handle it.
lines.ko: 아직. 내가 감당 못 한다고 생각할까 봐.

lines.text: Your health matters more. Maybe you should take a few days off.
lines.ko: 건강이 더 중요해. 며칠 쉬는 게 좋겠어.

response.situationKo: 친구가 요즘 너무 힘들다고 털어놓습니다. 위로하고 조언해 보세요.
response.prompt: I don't know, I just feel tired all the time lately.

answers.text: That sounds really hard. Maybe you should take a break this weekend.
I'm here if you want to talk. Want to grab dinner tonight?
It's okay to feel that way. Have you tried talking to someone about it?
Ugh, I'm sorry. Let's go for a walk and get some fresh air.

title: Can we talk about the kitchen?
settingKo: 설거지를 안 하는 룸메이트와 솔직하게 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hey, do you have a minute? I wanted to talk about the kitchen.
lines.ko: 잠깐 시간 돼? 부엌 얘기 좀 하고 싶어서.

lines.text: Sure. Is it the dishes again? Sorry, I've been super busy.
lines.ko: 그래. 또 설거지 때문이지? 미안, 요즘 너무 바빴어.

lines.text: I get it, but it's been a week. Maybe we could make a schedule?
lines.ko: 이해해. 그래도 일주일째야. 당번표를 만들면 어떨까?

lines.text: That's fair. How about I do weekdays and you do weekends?
lines.ko: 그게 맞지. 내가 평일, 네가 주말 하는 건 어때?

response.situationKo: 룸메이트가 밤늦게 친구를 자주 데려옵니다. 부드럽게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hey, what's up? You look like you want to say something.

answers.text: I was wondering if we could keep it quieter after eleven. I have work early.
answers.noteKo: I was wondering if는 아주 부드러운 부탁이에요.

answers.text: It's just that your friends stay pretty late, and I can't sleep.
answers.noteKo: It's just that은 조심스럽게 문제를 꺼내요.

answers.text: Could we maybe agree on no guests on weeknights?
Honestly, the late-night hangouts are getting a bit much for me.

title: Planning a trip together
settingKo: 친구와 여름휴가 여행지를 정합니다.

lines.text: So, beach or city? I'm leaning toward somewhere with a beach.
lines.ko: 그래서 바다 아니면 도시? 나는 바다 쪽으로 기울어.

lines.text: A beach sounds great, but I don't want it to be too crowded.
lines.ko: 바다 좋지, 근데 너무 붐비는 건 싫어.

lines.text: What about a small island in Thailand? Flights are cheap in June.
lines.ko: 태국의 작은 섬은 어때? 6월엔 비행기표가 싸.

lines.text: Isn't June the rainy season there? Let's check the weather first.
lines.ko: 6월이면 거기 우기 아니야? 날씨부터 확인해 보자.

response.situationKo: 친구가 여행 스타일을 묻습니다. 선호하는 걸 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What kind of trip do you prefer, relaxing or busy?

answers.text: I prefer relaxing trips. I just want to read by the pool.
I'd rather keep busy and see as much as possible.
A mix of both, honestly. Some sightseeing, some beach time.
answers.noteKo: a mix of both는 '둘 다 섞어서'예요.

answers.text: I enjoy a slower pace, with plenty of time to explore local food.

title: You should listen to this
settingKo: 동료에게 요즘 듣는 팟캐스트를 추천합니다.

lines.text: What do you listen to on your commute? You always have earbuds in.
lines.ko: 출퇴근할 때 뭐 들어? 맨날 이어폰 끼고 있던데.

lines.text: Mostly podcasts. Right now I'm into one about the history of food.
lines.ko: 주로 팟캐스트. 요즘은 음식의 역사에 대한 거에 빠져 있어.

lines.text: That sounds interesting. Is it easy to understand?
lines.ko: 재밌겠다. 알아듣기 쉬워?

lines.text: Yeah, the hosts speak clearly, and each episode is only twenty minutes.
lines.ko: 응, 진행자들이 또박또박 말하고 한 편이 20분밖에 안 돼.

response.situationKo: 친구가 요즘 빠져 있는 게 있는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: Are you into anything new these days?

answers.text: I'm really into pottery these days. I take a class on Saturdays.
I've been watching a lot of cooking videos lately.
I'm kind of obsessed with running now. I just signed up for a 10K.
I recently started learning the guitar. It's harder than I expected.

title: Could you give me a hand?
settingKo: 엑셀 작업이 막혀 동료에게 도움을 요청합니다.

lines.text: Sorry to interrupt. Could you give me a hand with this spreadsheet?
lines.ko: 방해해서 미안해요. 이 스프레드시트 좀 도와줄 수 있어요?

lines.text: Sure. What's the problem?
lines.ko: 그럼요. 뭐가 문제예요?

lines.text: The totals are wrong, and I can't figure out why.
lines.ko: 합계가 틀린데 왜 그런지 모르겠어요.

lines.text: Ah, I see. These cells are text, not numbers. Let me fix that.
lines.ko: 아, 알겠다. 이 칸들이 숫자가 아니라 텍스트예요. 제가 고칠게요.

phrases.en: Could you give me a hand?

response.situationKo: 동료가 도움을 요청하는데 지금은 바빠요. 나중에 돕겠다고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hey, do you have a few minutes to look at my slides?

answers.text: I'm in the middle of something. Can I look at them in twenty minutes?
answers.noteKo: in the middle of something은 '하던 중이야'예요.

answers.text: Sorry, I'm a bit busy right now, but I'm free after lunch.
Give me ten minutes and I'm all yours.
I have a call at three, but I can take a look after that.

title: Daily stand-up
settingKo: 매일 아침 짧은 팀 회의에서 진행 상황을 공유합니다.

lines.text: OK, let's go around. Min, what are you working on today?
lines.ko: 자, 돌아가면서 할게요. 민, 오늘 뭐 해요?

lines.text: Yesterday I finished the login page. Today I'm starting the payment screen.
lines.ko: 어제 로그인 페이지를 끝냈고, 오늘은 결제 화면을 시작해요.

lines.text: Great. Anything blocking you?
lines.ko: 좋아요. 막히는 건 없어요?

lines.text: Yes, I'm still waiting for the design files from the other team.
lines.ko: 네, 아직 다른 팀에서 디자인 파일을 기다리고 있어요.

phrases.en: What are you working on today?

response.situationKo: 아침 회의에서 내 진행 상황을 짧게 공유해 보세요.
response.prompt: Your turn. Quick update?

answers.text: Yesterday I finished the report. Today I'm working on the slides. No blockers.
answers.noteKo: 어제, 오늘, 막힌 것 순서가 기본이에요.

answers.text: I'm still working on the bug from Monday. I might need some help with it.
All good! Finished testing, and today I'm fixing small issues.
I finished the client email yesterday. Today I'll update the budget, but I'm blocked until finance replies.

title: Can I have a few more days?
settingKo: 마감을 지키기 어려워 상사에게 연장을 요청합니다.

lines.text: Do you have a second? I wanted to talk about the Friday deadline.
lines.ko: 잠깐 시간 되세요? 금요일 마감 얘기를 하고 싶어서요.

lines.text: Sure. Is there a problem?
lines.ko: 그래요. 문제가 있어요?

lines.text: The client changed the requirements, so I need two more days to do it properly.
lines.ko: 고객이 요구 사항을 바꿔서 제대로 하려면 이틀이 더 필요해요.

lines.text: OK, Tuesday is fine. Just send me a short update on Friday.
lines.ko: 좋아요, 화요일까지 괜찮아요. 금요일엔 짧게 진행 상황만 보내 줘요.

phrases.en: I wanted to talk about the deadline.
I need two more days to do it properly.

response.situationKo: 상사가 오늘까지 끝낼 수 있는지 묻는데 어려워요. 솔직하게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Can you have the report ready by the end of today?

answers.text: I'm afraid not. Could I send it tomorrow morning instead?
answers.noteKo: I'm afraid not은 정중한 '안 될 것 같아요'예요.

answers.text: Honestly, it'll be tight. I can send a draft today and the final tomorrow.
I need a bit more time. Is noon tomorrow OK?
Hmm, not today, sorry. First thing tomorrow?

title: How did I do?
settingKo: 발표가 끝나고 선배에게 피드백을 부탁합니다.

lines.text: Thanks for coming to my presentation. Do you have any feedback?
lines.ko: 발표 들어 주셔서 감사해요. 피드백 있으세요?

lines.text: Overall it was really clear. Your charts were easy to follow.
lines.ko: 전체적으로 아주 명확했어요. 그래프가 이해하기 쉬웠어요.

lines.text: One thing, though. You spoke a little fast at the beginning.
lines.ko: 다만 한 가지, 초반에 말이 조금 빨랐어요.

lines.text: That's helpful. I was nervous, so I'll practice slowing down.
lines.ko: 도움이 돼요. 긴장해서 그랬는데, 천천히 말하는 연습을 할게요.

response.situationKo: 동료가 자기 발표가 어땠는지 묻습니다. 좋은 점과 아쉬운 점을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Be honest. How was my presentation?

answers.text: It was great! I liked your examples. Maybe add a short summary at the end.
Really clear overall. One thing: try to look at the audience more.
Honestly, the content was strong, but the slides had a lot of text.
answers.noteKo: a lot of text는 글자가 많다는 거예요.

answers.text: I thought it went very well. Next time, you could leave more time for questions.

title: Which tools do we use?
settingKo: 새 회사에서 동료에게 업무 툴 사용법을 묻습니다.

lines.text: Quick question. Do people here use email or Slack for most things?
lines.ko: 질문 하나요. 여기선 주로 이메일 써요, 슬랙 써요?

lines.text: Mostly Slack. Email is only for clients and outside partners.
lines.ko: 거의 슬랙이요. 이메일은 고객이랑 외부 파트너용이에요.

lines.text: Got it. And where do we keep shared documents?
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 공유 문서는 어디에 둬요?

lines.text: Everything is in Google Drive. I'll add you to the team folder.
lines.ko: 다 구글 드라이브에 있어요. 팀 폴더에 추가해 줄게요.

phrases.en: I'll add you to the team folder.

response.situationKo: 새 동료가 업무에 대해 질문합니다. 하나 알려 주세요.
response.prompt: Sorry, how do I book a meeting room here?

answers.text: You can book it through the calendar app. Just add the room as a guest.
Let me show you. It only takes a minute.
Just use the booking page on the intranet. I'll send you the link.
Of course. You'll need to reserve it at least a day in advance.

title: Handling a complaint
settingKo: 매장 직원이 화난 고객의 불만을 듣습니다.

lines.text: This is the second time my order has been wrong. This is ridiculous.
lines.ko: 주문이 잘못된 게 벌써 두 번째예요. 말도 안 돼요.

lines.text: I completely understand, and I'm really sorry about that.
lines.ko: 충분히 이해합니다. 정말 죄송합니다.

lines.text: Let me fix it right now, and this one is on us.
lines.ko: 지금 바로 바로잡아 드리고, 이번 건은 저희가 부담할게요.

lines.text: OK. Thank you. I appreciate that.
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 고마워요. 그렇게 해 주시니 다행이네요.

response.situationKo: 고객이 배송이 늦다고 화를 냅니다. 사과하고 해결책을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: I've been waiting for my delivery for a week! Where is it?

answers.text: I'm really sorry about the delay. Let me check where your package is.
I completely understand your frustration. I'll call the delivery company right now.
I apologize for that. I'll send a new one with express shipping today.
Oh no, I'm so sorry. Can I have your order number so I can check?

title: A special dinner
settingKo: 기념일 저녁을 위해 식당에 전화로 예약합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'd like to book a table for two this Saturday at seven thirty.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 이번 토요일 7시 30분에 두 명 예약하고 싶어요.

lines.text: Let me check. We have a table at seven thirty, but it's near the kitchen.
lines.ko: 확인해 볼게요. 7시 30분 자리가 있는데 주방 근처예요.

lines.text: It's our anniversary. Is there anything quieter, maybe a little later?
lines.ko: 결혼기념일이라서요. 조금 늦더라도 더 조용한 자리 있을까요?

lines.text: There's a window table at eight fifteen. I'll add a note about the anniversary.
lines.ko: 8시 15분에 창가 자리가 있어요. 기념일이라고 메모해 둘게요.

phrases.en: I'd like to book a table for two.

response.situationKo: 식당 직원이 특별한 요청이 있는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: Is there anything special we should know about your booking?

answers.text: It's my wife's birthday. Could you bring a small cake with a candle?
One of us is vegetarian, so please let the chef know.
answers.noteKo: let the chef know는 '셰프에게 알려 주세요'예요.

answers.text: We're bringing a baby, so we'll need a high chair.
Just a quiet table if possible. It's kind of a big night for us.

title: I'm trying to eat less meat
settingKo: 친구에게 고기를 줄이고 있다고 이야기합니다.

lines.text: You didn't order the steak? That's not like you.
lines.ko: 스테이크 안 시켰어? 너답지 않네.

lines.text: I'm trying to eat less meat. I feel lighter and I sleep better.
lines.ko: 고기를 줄이는 중이야. 몸이 가볍고 잠도 더 잘 와.

lines.text: Isn't it hard to get enough protein, though?
lines.ko: 그래도 단백질 충분히 먹기 어렵지 않아?

lines.text: Not really. I eat a lot of tofu, beans, and eggs now.
lines.ko: 별로. 요즘 두부, 콩, 달걀을 많이 먹어.

phrases.en: I'm trying to eat less meat.

response.situationKo: 친구가 요즘 건강을 위해 바꾼 습관이 있는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: Have you changed anything to be healthier lately?

answers.text: I've started walking to work instead of taking the bus.
I'm trying to drink less coffee. Only one cup a day now.
I quit eating late at night. It really helped my sleep.
I've been cooking at home more often rather than ordering delivery.

title: Are you coming to the wedding?
settingKo: 친구 결혼식 초대에 참석 여부를 답합니다.

lines.text: Did you get our wedding invitation? We need to know the numbers by Friday.
lines.ko: 우리 청첩장 받았어? 금요일까지 인원을 알아야 해서.

lines.text: Yes! I'd love to come. Is it OK if I bring my boyfriend?
lines.ko: 응! 꼭 갈게. 남자친구 데려가도 돼?

lines.text: Of course. Just let me know if either of you has any food restrictions.
lines.ko: 당연하지. 둘 중에 못 먹는 음식 있으면 알려 줘.

lines.text: He doesn't eat seafood, but other than that we're fine.
lines.ko: 남자친구가 해산물을 안 먹는데, 그 외엔 괜찮아.

phrases.en: Is it OK if I bring my boyfriend?

response.situationKo: 친구 결혼식에 갈 수 없어요. 아쉬움을 담아 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, can you make it to the wedding in June?

answers.text: I'm so sorry, I can't. I'll be abroad for work that week.
Unfortunately, I can't make it, but congratulations! I'll send a gift.
Ugh, I wish I could! My sister's graduation is the same day.
answers.noteKo: I wish I could는 '갈 수 있으면 좋겠는데'예요.

answers.text: I'm really sorry to miss it. Let's celebrate together when I'm back.

title: Signing up to volunteer
settingKo: 동물 보호소 봉사 활동을 신청합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I saw on Instagram that you're looking for volunteers.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 인스타에서 봉사자를 구한다고 봤어요.

lines.text: Yes, we need help walking the dogs on weekends. Do you have any experience?
lines.ko: 네, 주말에 개 산책을 도와줄 분이 필요해요. 경험 있으세요?

lines.text: I grew up with two dogs, so I'm comfortable with big ones too.
lines.ko: 개 두 마리랑 같이 자라서 큰 개도 괜찮아요.

lines.text: Perfect. Come to our training session next Saturday at ten.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 다음 주 토요일 10시 교육에 오세요.

response.situationKo: 담당자가 왜 봉사를 하고 싶은지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: What made you want to volunteer with us?

answers.text: I love animals, and I want to do something useful on weekends.
answers.noteKo: do something useful은 보람 있는 일을 하는 거예요.

answers.text: I'd like to give back to my community.
answers.noteKo: give back은 받은 걸 돌려주는 거예요.

answers.text: Honestly, I work from home and I need a reason to get outside!
Because I adopted my cat from a shelter, and I want to help others do the same.

title: Can you help me move?
settingKo: 친구에게 이사를 도와 달라고 부탁합니다.

lines.text: I'm moving next Sunday. Any chance you could help me carry some boxes?
lines.ko: 다음 주 일요일에 이사해. 혹시 짐 좀 같이 날라 줄 수 있어?

lines.text: Sure. Are you hiring movers, or are we doing everything ourselves?
lines.ko: 그럼. 이삿짐센터 불러, 아니면 우리끼리 다 해?

lines.text: Movers are coming for the furniture. I just need help with the small stuff.
lines.ko: 가구는 이삿짐센터가 와. 작은 짐만 도와주면 돼.

lines.text: No problem. Pizza and drinks after, right?
lines.ko: 문제없어. 끝나고 피자랑 음료는 있는 거지?

phrases.en: Any chance you could help me?
I just need help with the small stuff.

response.situationKo: 친구가 이사를 도와 달라는데 그날 일정이 있어요. 다른 방법을 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: Can you help me move this Saturday?

answers.text: I can't on Saturday, but I could help you pack on Friday night.
Sorry, I have plans, but how about I bring dinner on Sunday?
answers.noteKo: how about I로 대신할 일을 제안해요.

answers.text: I'm afraid I'm busy that day. Would it help if I lent you my car?
answers.noteKo: Would it help if는 정중한 제안이에요.

answers.text: Saturday is tough, but I'm free in the afternoon. Is that too late?

title: Is this still available?
settingKo: 중고 거래 앱에서 자전거를 사려고 판매자와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hi, is the bike still available? I saw it on the app.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 자전거 아직 있나요? 앱에서 봤어요.

lines.text: Yes, it is. It's two years old, but I barely used it.
lines.ko: 네, 있어요. 2년 됐는데 거의 안 탔어요.

lines.text: Would you take one hundred and fifty instead of two hundred?
lines.ko: 200 말고 150에 주실 수 있나요?

lines.text: How about one seventy? And I'll throw in the lock.
lines.ko: 170은 어때요? 자물쇠도 같이 드릴게요.

response.situationKo: 물건을 팔고 있는데 구매자가 깎아 달라고 합니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Would you take forty dollars for the chair?

answers.text: Sorry, the lowest I can go is fifty.
answers.noteKo: the lowest I can go는 '최대로 깎으면'이에요.

answers.text: How about forty-five? It's almost new.
Deal! When can you pick it up?
I'm sorry, but the price is firm. It's already a good deal.

title: Sharing an account
settingKo: 친구와 영상 구독 서비스를 나눠 쓰는 이야기를 합니다.

lines.text: Are you still paying for three streaming services? That's a lot every month.
lines.ko: 아직 스트리밍 서비스 세 개 내? 매달 꽤 많잖아.

lines.text: I know. I only really watch one of them, to be honest.
lines.ko: 알아. 솔직히 하나만 제대로 봐.

lines.text: Why don't we share a family plan? It's cheaper if we split it.
lines.ko: 우리 가족 요금제 같이 쓸래? 나누면 더 싸.

lines.text: Good idea. I'll cancel the other two this weekend.
lines.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 나머지 두 개는 이번 주말에 해지할게.

phrases.en: To be honest, I only watch one.
It's cheaper if we split it.

response.situationKo: 친구가 쓸데없이 나가는 돈이 있냐고 묻습니다. 줄이고 싶은 걸 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's something you spend too much money on?

answers.text: Probably food delivery. I order almost every night.
Coffee! I spend like five dollars a day on lattes.
I spend too much on clothes I don't really need.
Taxis, honestly. I should take the subway more often.

title: Which phone should I get?
settingKo: 전자 제품 매장 직원에게 휴대폰 추천을 받습니다.

lines.text: I need a new phone, but I'm not sure which one to get.
lines.ko: 새 휴대폰이 필요한데 어떤 걸 사야 할지 모르겠어요.

lines.text: What's most important to you? Camera, battery, or price?
lines.ko: 뭐가 제일 중요하세요? 카메라, 배터리, 가격?

lines.text: Battery, definitely. My current phone dies before lunch.
lines.ko: 무조건 배터리요. 지금 폰은 점심 전에 꺼져요.

lines.text: Then this one is great. It easily lasts two days on one charge.
lines.ko: 그럼 이게 좋아요. 한 번 충전으로 이틀은 거뜬해요.

phrases.en: I'm not sure which one to get.
It lasts two days on one charge.

response.situationKo: 직원이 비싼 모델을 권합니다. 예산이 있다고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: This is our newest model. It's twelve hundred dollars.

answers.text: That's a bit out of my budget. Do you have something under six hundred?
answers.noteKo: out of my budget은 예산 초과예요.

answers.text: Hmm, too expensive for me. Anything cheaper?
It looks great, but I don't need all those features. What about last year's model?
I'd like to spend around five hundred at most.

title: She broke up with me
settingKo: 최근 이별한 친구를 위로합니다.

lines.text: I heard about you and Jess. How are you holding up?
lines.ko: 너랑 제스 얘기 들었어. 좀 괜찮아?

lines.text: Honestly, not great. We were together for three years.
lines.ko: 솔직히 별로야. 3년이나 사귀었잖아.

lines.text: That's really tough. Do you want to get out of the house this weekend?
lines.ko: 정말 힘들겠다. 이번 주말에 바람 좀 쐬러 갈래?

lines.text: Yeah, that would help. I've just been sitting at home.
lines.ko: 응, 그게 도움이 될 것 같아. 계속 집에만 있었거든.

response.situationKo: 친구가 시험에 떨어졌다고 합니다. 위로해 보세요.
response.prompt: I didn't pass the exam. I studied so hard for it.

answers.text: I'm so sorry. You worked really hard, and I'm proud of you.
That's really tough. You'll get it next time, I'm sure.
Ugh, that sucks. Let me buy you dinner tonight.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Let me know if there's anything I can do.

title: Calling home
settingKo: 해외에 사는 자녀가 부모님과 영상 통화를 합니다.

lines.text: You look thin. Are you eating properly over there?
lines.ko: 너 살 빠져 보인다. 거기서 밥은 잘 먹니?

lines.text: Yes, Mom, I cook almost every night now. Don't worry.
lines.ko: 네, 엄마, 요즘은 거의 매일 밤 요리해요. 걱정 마세요.

lines.text: Good. Are you coming home for the holidays this year?
lines.ko: 다행이다. 올해 명절엔 집에 오니?

lines.text: I'm planning to, but the flights are really expensive right now.
lines.ko: 그럴 계획인데 지금 비행기표가 너무 비싸요.

gist.questionKo: 집에 가는 데 문제가 되는 것은?

response.situationKo: 부모님이 요즘 어떻게 지내는지 물으십니다. 근황을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, how's everything going? Tell us about your week.

answers.text: It's been busy, but good. Work is going well.
I've been working a lot, but I went hiking with friends on Sunday.
Pretty good! I finally found a Korean restaurant near my place.
Everything's fine. Please don't worry too much about me.

title: This heat is crazy
settingKo: 동료와 기록적인 더위에 대해 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Did you see it hit thirty-nine degrees yesterday? That's a new record.
lines.ko: 어제 39도 찍은 거 봤어? 신기록이래.

lines.text: I know. My apartment doesn't have AC, so I couldn't sleep at all.
lines.ko: 그러니까. 우리 집에 에어컨이 없어서 한숨도 못 잤어.

lines.text: Summers seem to get hotter every year.
lines.ko: 여름이 매년 더 더워지는 것 같아.

lines.text: Seriously. I'm thinking of working from the library this week.
lines.ko: 진짜. 이번 주엔 도서관에서 일할까 생각 중이야.

gist.questionKo: 두 번째 사람이 잠을 못 잔 이유는?

phrases.en: Summers seem to get hotter every year.
phrases.ko: 여름이 매년 더 더워지는 것 같아.

response.situationKo: 친구가 더위를 어떻게 견디는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: How are you surviving this heat?

answers.text: I'm staying inside as much as possible and drinking lots of water.
Barely! I take like three cold showers a day.
I've been going to cafés with air conditioning to work.
I bought a portable fan. It helps a little, at least.

title: The trains are on strike
settingKo: 지하철 파업으로 출근 방법을 동료와 의논합니다.

lines.text: Did you hear? The subway workers are on strike tomorrow.
lines.ko: 들었어? 내일 지하철 파업이래.

lines.text: Oh no. How long is it going to last?
lines.ko: 이런. 얼마나 간대?

lines.text: Just one day, but the buses will be packed. Want to share a taxi?
lines.ko: 하루만인데 버스가 꽉 찰 거야. 택시 같이 탈래?

lines.text: Sure, or maybe the boss will let us work from home.
lines.ko: 좋아, 아니면 팀장님이 재택근무하게 해 줄지도 몰라.

phrases.en: How long is it going to last?

response.situationKo: 출근길이 막혀 회의에 늦을 것 같아요. 팀에 메시지를 보내 보세요.
response.prompt: Team chat: Morning everyone! Meeting starts in ten minutes.

answers.text: Sorry, I'm stuck in traffic. Please start without me.
Running about fifteen minutes late because of the strike. I'll join online.
Apologies, the buses are packed. I'll be there as soon as I can.
answers.noteKo: as soon as I can은 '최대한 빨리'예요.

answers.text: Ugh, traffic is insane. Save me a seat!
answers.noteKo: Save me a seat은 '자리 맡아 줘'예요.

title: Can we swap shifts?
settingKo: 카페 아르바이트생이 동료에게 근무를 바꿔 달라고 부탁합니다.

lines.text: Hey, would you be able to swap shifts with me next Saturday?
lines.ko: 다음 주 토요일 근무 나랑 바꿔 줄 수 있어?

lines.text: Maybe. What's going on?
lines.ko: 아마도. 무슨 일인데?

lines.text: My cousin is getting married, and I totally forgot to ask for the day off.
lines.ko: 사촌이 결혼하는데 쉬는 날 신청하는 걸 완전히 잊었어.

lines.text: OK, I'll take your Saturday if you take my Monday morning.
lines.ko: 알았어, 네가 내 월요일 오전 맡아 주면 토요일 맡을게.

phrases.en: Would you be able to swap shifts?
I forgot to ask for the day off.

response.situationKo: 동료가 근무를 바꿔 달라는데 그날 안 돼요. 다른 날을 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: Could you cover my shift on Friday night?

answers.text: Sorry, I can't on Friday, but I could do Thursday if that helps.
Friday's tough for me. Maybe ask Jake? He wanted more hours.
I'm afraid I already have plans. What about Sunday instead?
I can cover the first half, until nine. Would that work?

title: I got a parking ticket
settingKo: 주차 위반 딱지에 대해 시청 직원에게 문의합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I got a parking ticket, but I think it's a mistake.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 주차 딱지를 받았는데 착오인 것 같아요.

lines.text: OK. Why do you think it's a mistake?
lines.ko: 네. 왜 착오라고 생각하세요?

lines.text: I paid for two hours on the app, and I was back after ninety minutes.
lines.ko: 앱으로 두 시간 결제했고 90분 만에 돌아왔어요.

lines.text: If you send us a screenshot of the payment, we can cancel it.
lines.ko: 결제 화면을 캡처해서 보내 주시면 취소해 드릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Send us a screenshot of the payment.

response.situationKo: 요금이 잘못 청구됐어요. 고객센터에 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Customer service, how can I help?

answers.text: I was charged twice for the same order. Could you check, please?
My bill is higher than usual, and I think there's a mistake.
Hi, I canceled last month, but you still charged me.
There's a fee on my statement that I don't recognize.

title: My dog isn't eating
settingKo: 밥을 안 먹는 강아지를 데리고 동물병원에 갑니다.

lines.text: So what's been going on with Mochi?
lines.ko: 모찌는 어떤 증상이 있었나요?

lines.text: He hasn't eaten anything since yesterday, and he seems really tired.
lines.ko: 어제부터 아무것도 안 먹고 많이 지쳐 보여요.

lines.text: Has he eaten anything unusual, like chocolate or a toy?
lines.ko: 초콜릿이나 장난감 같은 이상한 걸 먹었나요?

lines.text: Actually, I think he chewed one of my socks.
lines.ko: 사실 제 양말 하나를 씹은 것 같아요.

lines.text: OK, let's do an X-ray to make sure nothing is stuck.
lines.ko: 네, 뭐가 걸려 있지 않은지 엑스레이를 찍어 볼게요.

phrases.en: He hasn't eaten anything since yesterday.
Let's make sure nothing is stuck.
phrases.ko: 뭐가 걸려 있지 않은지 확인해 봐요.

response.situationKo: 수의사가 반려동물 상태를 묻습니다. 증상을 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: What symptoms have you noticed?

answers.text: She's been throwing up since this morning.
He's been scratching his ear a lot, and it looks red.
He's limping on his back leg. I think he hurt it at the park.
She's not eating and just sleeps all day. It's not like her.
answers.noteKo: It's not like her는 '평소 같지 않다'예요.

title: Leaving a review
settingKo: 여행 후 친구와 숙소 후기를 어떻게 쓸지 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Are you going to leave a review for the apartment?
lines.ko: 숙소 후기 남길 거야?

lines.text: Yes. The location was perfect, but the bed was really uncomfortable.
lines.ko: 응. 위치는 완벽했는데 침대가 진짜 불편했어.

lines.text: Should we mention the noise from the bar downstairs?
lines.ko: 아래층 술집 소음도 쓸까?

lines.text: Definitely. Other guests should know before they book.
lines.ko: 당연하지. 다른 손님들이 예약 전에 알아야지.

phrases.en: Other guests should know before they book.

response.situationKo: 다녀온 식당 후기를 말로 남겨 보세요. 좋은 점과 아쉬운 점을 모두요.
response.prompt: So how would you describe the restaurant to someone else?

answers.text: The food was amazing, but the service was a little slow.
I'd recommend it for a date. It's a bit pricey, though.
Honestly, worth the wait! Just go early because it gets packed.
The atmosphere was lovely, although the portions were rather small.

title: How do you study?
settingKo: 영어를 잘하는 친구에게 공부 방법을 묻습니다.

lines.text: Your English is so natural. How did you get so good?
lines.ko: 너 영어 진짜 자연스럽다. 어떻게 그렇게 잘하게 됐어?

lines.text: Honestly, I just talked a lot, even when I made mistakes.
lines.ko: 솔직히 그냥 많이 말했어, 틀려도.

lines.text: I'm always scared of sounding stupid.
lines.ko: 나는 늘 바보같이 들릴까 봐 무서워.

lines.text: Everyone feels that way at first. Try shadowing short videos every day.
lines.ko: 처음엔 다 그래. 매일 짧은 영상을 따라 말해 봐.

phrases.en: How did you get so good?
Everyone feels that way at first.

response.situationKo: 친구가 외국어 공부 팁을 묻습니다. 하나 알려 주세요.
response.prompt: Any tips for learning a language faster?

answers.text: Try to speak a little every day, even just to yourself.
What helped me was changing my phone language to English.
answers.noteKo: What helped me was로 경험을 말해요.

answers.text: Don't worry about mistakes. Just keep talking!
You should find something you enjoy, like a show, and study with it.

title: I can't take this on
settingKo: 이미 바쁜데 상사가 일을 더 맡기려 합니다.

lines.text: Could you also take over the newsletter this month? Ella is on leave.
lines.ko: 이번 달 뉴스레터도 맡아 줄 수 있어요? 엘라가 휴가라서요.

lines.text: I'd like to help, but I'm already working on two big projects.
lines.ko: 돕고 싶은데 이미 큰 프로젝트 두 개를 하고 있어요.

lines.text: If I take it on, one of them might be late. Which one is more important?
lines.ko: 제가 맡으면 둘 중 하나가 늦어질 수 있어요. 어떤 게 더 중요할까요?

lines.text: Good point. Let's ask Ryan to do the newsletter instead.
lines.ko: 맞는 말이에요. 뉴스레터는 라이언에게 부탁할게요.

phrases.en: I'd like to help, but I'm already working on two projects.
phrases.ko: 돕고 싶은데 이미 프로젝트 두 개를 하고 있어요.

response.situationKo: 동료가 또 일을 부탁합니다. 정중하게 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hey, could you handle this client call for me tomorrow?

answers.text: I'd love to help, but my plate is really full this week.
answers.noteKo: my plate is full은 '할 일이 꽉 찼어'예요.

answers.text: I'm afraid I can't tomorrow. I'm in workshops all day.
answers.noteKo: I'm afraid I can't는 정중한 거절이에요.

answers.text: Sorry, not this time! Maybe next week?
I can't take the call, but I can send you my notes from last time.
answers.noteKo: 할 수 있는 일을 대신 제안해요.
